title: String Theory export
description: One JSON file per application. Exports the app's own UI strings with a pixel budget so a human can rewrite them and the app can merge the rewrites back by id. Canonical form only: the loader also accepts documented aliases, but an exporter should emit exactly these names.

format.description: Format id. Optional on input, always written on output.

app.description: Application name. Shown in the header, used for the export filename.

context.description: One line about the screen or feature, sent with every AI prompt.

defaultMaxPx.description: Pixel budget for strings that do not carry their own maxPx.

font.description: The font the pixel figures are measured in. Must match what the app renders with.

family.description: Font family name, for example 'Segoe UI'. Fallback stacks are allowed.

weight.description: Numeric weight preferred. Strings are wider at heavier weights.

letterSpacing.description: Extra tracking in CSS pixels, added per character.

id.description: Stable id from the app catalogue. Unique per file.

text.description: The string as it ships today. Keep it on one line; a newline is measured at the widest line.

where.description: The line of UI where the string appears. Shown on hover and sent to the model.

maxPx.description: Pixel width the line must not exceed, measured in the file font.

maxChars.description: Character ceiling, only when the app enforces one itself.

px.description: Optional: the app's own measurement. Only used for the budget when maxPx is absent.
